BNN responds same day: neither had occurred. BNN Network (BNN) response at 4:37 PM confirms facts. Feb. 27 at 9:22 AM: BNN submits telehealth accommodation request to CDCR.

Agent Moua calls BNN at 1:36 PM (55 seconds, from +1(510)227-9994 — IMG_7328.png) and directs BNN to cease in-person attendance at HOPE Psychotherapy and instead attend telehealth sessions with Pam Akins beginning March 31, 2026. At 2:07 PM BNN texts Kelly Phaysaleum at HOPE to confirm no in-person attendance required; Kelly's 2:14 PM response: 'Please contact your agent' — confirming HOPE was not formally notified of the telehealth transition by Moua

Agent Moua texts BNN at 3:24 PM: 'Starts 3/31/26 / Telehealth for HOPE / Tuesdays/Thursdays / 9AM-1030AM / Call 617-675-4444.' At 3:29 PM BNN replies: 'Is there an Access Code for this conference call I should be aware of?' — Moua never responds to the access code request. This unreturned question becomes the central document in the fabricated violation that follows.

First scheduled telehealth session. At 9:01 AM BNN texts Moua: 'Agent Moua, please provide me with the Google pin needed to enter the call.' Moua does not respond. BNN is unable to enter the conference call without the access code and cannot attend the session. The non-attendance — caused by Moua's failure to provide the access code — is subsequently submitted by Moua as a willful 'failure to attend treatment' parole violation.

Agent Moua texts BNN at 9:35 AM: 'Come to the office.' At the parole office, Moua questions BNN about the missed March 31 telehealth session. BNN states he attempted to obtain the access code. Moua claims he provided it — a claim directly contradicted by the text record (no access code was ever transmitted). Moua states affirmatively he will submit 'failure to attend treatment' as a violation into the parole system. This is the fabrication event: Moua creates a false administrative record to manufacture pretext for future adverse action.

RETALIATORY TRANSFER — Agent Moua calls BNN to report to Stockton parole office for urine sample. After UA, Moua announces BNN's file is being transferred to Santa Clara Parole GPS Unit. Moua's stated reason: 'Too many violations.' The March 31 fabricated telehealth violation — manufactured by Moua — is among the violations cited. Transfer order issued 18 days after lawsuit filing (Jun. 11) and 7 days after service on CDCR/Dodd (Jun. 22); temporal proximity is the strongest possible evidence of retaliatory motive.

No documented permission granted. At 6:05 PM July 6, BNN texts Brown confirming sex offender registration complete and Amazon job details (IMG_7326.png). Macy's (Stockton, ~60+ miles from Santa Clara GPS Unit) immediately becomes inaccessible.
